items.headline: Why Washington Is Treating Rare Earths Like Gold
items.snippet: Albemarle Corporation (ALB) remains the largest publicly traded globally, with a geographically diversified asset base spanning Australian hard-rock spodumene operations, Chilean brine production in the Salar de Atacama, and the Silver Peak facility in Nevada.

items.headline: Albemarle Appoints Former Vale CEO Eduardo Bartolomeo as Outside Director
items.snippet: Albemarle (ALB) appointed Eduardo Bartolomeo, former Vale CEO, as an outside director effective July 21st, seen as strengthening lithium production expansion and supply chain strategy.

items.headline: Albemarle Stock Loses 25% in a Month: What Should Investors Do Now?
items.snippet: Albemarle Corporation's ALB shares have tumbled 25.5% in the past month, underperforming the Zacks Chemical - Diversified industry and the S&P 500. Falling lithium market prices are weighing on the ALB stock lately.

items.headline: The U.S. Is Increasing Efforts to Rebuild Its Rare Earth Supply Chain
items.snippet: Albemarle's Q1 2026 adjusted EBITDA jumped 148% YoY to $664 million as lithium prices rebounded from 2025 lows; the company retired $1.3 billion of debt during the quarter.

items.headline: Lithium Is on the Rise Again. Does That Make Albemarle a Buy?
items.snippet: Chinese spot lithium prices have climbed back into the $23/kg range, up from a $10/kg low in fall 2024. Analysts project a 4% global lithium supply deficit for 2026.
